en: Salutations be to the abode of Nārāyaṇa; salutations be to the one whose neck is adorned with a necklace of souls;
salutations be to the one celebrated as the ultimate goal; salutations be to you, O Nārāyaṇa, who are worshipped by all. || 1 ||
Salutation be to the Fish who dwells in the ocean of dissolution; salutation be to the Tortoise who dwells in the milk-ocean;
salutation to the Boar, the upholder of the earth; salutation to Nṛsiṃha, who is higher than the highest. || 2 ||
Salutations to the one who became Vāmana by taking refuge in Śakra; salutations to Bhārgava, the joy of the brahmins;
salutations to Rāghava, the benefactor of Sītā; salutations to the Yādava praised by Pārtha. || 3 ||
Homage be to the Buddha who dispels delusion; homage be to you, who have arisen from the Kalki age;
homage be to the one possessed of infinite and perfect virtues, the Lord of all, Hayagrīva. || 4 ||

Homage be to Hayānana, who holds in his hands a conch, a shimmering rosary, the gesture of reassurance, and a book; who proclaims the Āgamas from his mouth; and who has cast away all that is to be abandoned.

Salutations to the horse-faced one (Hayānana), who is attended in the four directions by the four forms of Ramā, and who is consecrated by the glory of the two-formed [goddess] situated on his two flanks.

Salutations be to you, Hayānana, whose limbs are resplendent with a crown, a turban, armlets, necklaces, a girdle, a golden-yellow garment, anklets, and other ornaments, and who are surrounded by the gods.
Homage be to the horse-faced one (Hayānana), who is worthy of praise by the liberated, who has shaken off all obstacles from every side;
homage be to him whose deeds are praised in the eightfold hymns composed by Vādirāja, the bestower of desires upon the virtuous.
Homage be to the one whose deeds are praised by the eightfold hymns of Vādirāja, the bestower of desires upon the learned;
to the horse-headed one (Hayānana) residing within the orb of the moon, who grants the aims of the gods through his ten incarnations.
Thus ends the *Daśāvatārastotra* composed by the venerable Vādirāja.
